requiredFindings.title: Check held-out identities, not only the number of rows, in the Rust margin test
requiredFindings.finding: The claimed coverage check counts outstanding/stale/measured/error rows and requires a total of ten, but never checks unique IDs or compares those IDs with the expected held-out manifest set. Ten composed passing rows all carrying the same ID, or a foreign ID replacing one expected entry, still satisfy these checks and yield holds (blind census) with gate=true. The Python receipt composer checks identities correctly, but the separately requested product margin test does not independently verify the composed artifact. The partial-coverage negative tests only the count, not same-count substitutions or duplicates.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Bind the Rust control to the expected held-out ID set from reviewed manifest evidence, reject duplicates and missing/unknown/substituted IDs, and ensure held-out statuses cannot replace lead-readable rows. Add same-count duplicate-ID and foreign-ID census-record negatives, plus an omitted lead-readable row/status-substitution control. Only exact coverage with all expected successful measurements may meet the gate.

requiredFindings.title: Close the SystemExit and blind-mode detection gaps in exception redaction
requiredFindings.finding: blind_row catches Exception, which excludes SystemExit, while __main__ explicitly rethrows SystemExit before the generic blind-mode redaction branch. A verification/model/helper exit such as SystemExit(secret_path) therefore reaches Python termination handling, which prints that string to stderr. In addition, the redaction guard detects only the exact literal --held-out-blind in argv, while argparse permits abbreviated long options by default; an accepted abbreviation enters blind mode without setting this guard. The current CLI canary only exercises an OSError with the full flag and misses both paths. This contradicts the before-run requirement that exceptions, including top-level ones, never disclose content.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Put the actual parsed blind execution behind a redaction boundary that also sanitizes message-bearing SystemExit, distinguishing intentional parser/help exits before any held-out access. Make dispatch/redaction agree for every accepted flag spelling, for example by disabling abbreviation and dispatching from parsed arguments. Add synthetic/subprocess canaries for SystemExit carrying a planted name/path and for accepted/rejected abbreviated flags; verify stderr/stdout contain only the permitted summary or generic failure, with no exception text.

requiredFindings.title: Bind or verify the imported population-loader dependency before reusing a receipt
requiredFindings.finding: receipt_bindings covers the census script and Rust cost closure but omits tools/security/discovery_walk_vectors.py, which load_reference imports and executes. That helper selects and loads the reference through ARCH/load, supplies MARKERS to reference_population, and reads the Python generator-closure configuration. Changing that helper can change the population/reference check while leaving every receipt binding unchanged; compose_held_out then continues to accept the old receipt as current. Existing drift controls change only already-bound inputs and do not exercise this executable dependency. The saved result is therefore not bound to all code that performed its population verification.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Include the imported helper and relevant reference/loading dependency pins in the receipt binding, or enforce their fixed accepted hashes before either a blind run or ordinary receipt reuse. Account for the configuration/closure inputs selecting executed reference dependencies. Use only public code/input pins, preserving the disclosure limit. Add a synthetic helper/reference-loader drift control showing that an old receipt becomes stale or is refused before composition, without opening a held-out store.
